subject.title: [Bug]: codex harness mirrored-session-history read fails for ephemeral sessions and on failover; one-shot cleanup retires shared app-server client while turns are in flight

question: What permanent ownership model should OpenClaw use for Codex one-shot cleanup and cross-provider fallback history when a Codex app-server turn fails mid-flight?
rationale: A narrow parser or warning change will not settle whether one-shot runs should use isolated clients, shared-client refcounts, delayed retirement, or a broader transcript handoff; replay and fallback behavior can affect user-visible message loss and side-effect safety.

options.title: Own the lifecycle repair
options.body: Treat this as a maintainer-owned Codex runtime fix covering shared-client leases, one-shot cleanup, transcript parsing/skipping, and fallback handoff together.

options.title: Split into narrower issues
options.body: Keep this issue as the umbrella and explicitly move `session_meta`, shared-client retirement, and fallback transcript continuity into separate canonical issues before implementation.

options.title: Limit scope to warning noise
options.body: Accept the merged missing-file fix as enough for warnings and leave shared-client/fallback behavior to existing broader app-server close reports.

recommendation.title: Own the lifecycle repair
recommendation.body: Treat this as a maintainer-owned Codex runtime fix covering shared-client leases, one-shot cleanup, transcript parsing/skipping, and fallback handoff together.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the most recent shared-client/thread ownership signal and are a good routing point for the lifecycle policy choice.
